knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=RNA-seq read coverage matrix or GRanges object representing genomic regions ;; classlabel=vector of cluster labels for the samples being tested
- alternatives: sigclust=the underlying statistical framework, which SigFuge adapts specifically for genomic coverage data
- when_to_use: Use when you have clustered RNA-seq samples based on locus-level read coverage and want to determine if the clusters represent statistically significant biological subgroups rather than random variation.
- pitfalls: The package is deprecated and has been removed from the active Bioconductor release (3.23), requiring legacy R/Bioconductor environments for installation and execution.

workflows.name: sigfuge_significance_testing
workflows.intent: Cluster RNA-seq coverage data and test the statistical significance of the resulting clusters.
input: coverage_data.RData (matrix of locus-level RNA-seq read coverage across samples)
clusters.csv (pre-defined or computed sample cluster assignments)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the coverage data and cluster assignments ;; 2. Visualize the coverage curves across clusters using sfPlot ;; 3. Cluster the coverage curves using sfCluster ;; 4. Test the significance of the clusters using sfSignificance
